REZ-2026101999 Fairfield REZ-2026101530 Fairfield REZ-2026101524 Brookland Rudlin Torah Academy: Request to conditionally rezone from O-3C Office District (Conditional) to B-1C Business District (Conditional) part of Parcel 778-757-8541 containing 2.6 acres located at the southeast intersection of E. Parham Road and Lydell Drive. The applicant proposes a private school. The use will be controlled by zoning ordinance regulations and proffered conditions. The 2045 Comprehensive Plan recommends Office and Environmental Protection Area. Acting on a motion by Mr. Dandridge, seconded by Mr. Winterhoff, the Planning Commission voted 5-0 (one abstention) to recommend the Board of Supervisors grant the request because it would permit infill development with the proper connection for roads and other public facilities. Ridge Homes LLC: Request to conditionally rezone from B-3C Business District (Conditional) to R-6C General Residence District (Conditional) Parcel 784-747-2895 containing 2.00 acres located on the north line of Brook Lake Drive approximately 500’ west of its intersection with Brook Road (US Route 1). The applicant proposes residential condominiums. The use will be controlled by zoning ordinance regulations and proffered conditions. The 2045 Comprehensive Plan recommends Multi-Family Residential. The site is located in the Enterprise Zone. Acting on a motion by Mr. Dandridge, seconded by Mr. Winterhoff, the Planning Commission voted 5-0 (one abstention) to recommend the Board of Supervisors deny the request because the applicant failed to meet their burden to show that the requested changes are in the best interests of the welfare and future of the community. (Deferral requested to the second January 2027, meeting.) Woodman Investment Company LLC: Request to conditionally rezone from A-1 Agricultural District to R-5AC General Residence District (Conditional) Parcels 772-771-3063 and 772-772-8610 containing 14.94 acres located at the northwest intersection of Braxton Avenue and Quail Walk Drive. The applicant proposes single-family development. The use will be controlled by zoning ordinance regulations and proffered conditions. The 2045 Comprehensive Plan recommends Suburban Residential 2 (density should not exceed 5 units per acre), Environmental Protection Area, and Suburban Residential 1 (density should not exceed 3 units per acre). Acting on a motion by Mr. Phelps, seconded by Mr. Shippee, the Planning Commission voted 5-0 (one abstention) to recommend the Board of Supervisors deny the request because it would likely set an adverse zoning and land use precedent for the area. (Deferral requested the second January 2027, meeting.) Public Hearings - Other Items Ordinance - To Add Article XIV, Titled “Marijuana Sales Tax,” to Chapter 20 of the Code of the County of Henrico to Tax the Sale of Marijuana and Marijuana Products at a Rate of Three and One-Half Percent in Accordance with State Law. This Board paper proposes ordinance amendments to levy a local marijuana sales tax at the rate of three and one-half percent on any sale of any marijuana or marijuana products in 2 accordance with state law. State law currently requires the rate to remain in effect for at least three years. The Finance Director recommends approval of this Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. Ordinance - To Amend and Reordain Section 13-27 Titled “Reserved” of the Code of the County of Henrico to Prohibit Consuming Marijuana or Marijuana Products, or Offering to Another, in Certain Public Places; Prohibit Consuming or Possessing Marijuana or Marijuana Products in or on Public School Grounds; and Regulate the Time of Sale of Marijuana or Marijuana Products. This Board paper proposes ordinance amendments to prohibit consuming marijuana or marijuana products, or offering marijuana or marijuana products to others, in public parks, playgrounds, public streets, or any sidewalk adjoining any public street. The amendments also prohibit consuming or possessing marijuana or marijuana products in or on public school grounds. Finally, the amendments establish hours during which marijuana and marijuana products may be sold by retail marijuana stores and microbusinesses licensed by the Virginia Cannabis Control Authority. The Chief of Police recommends approval of this Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. Ordinance - To Amend and Reordain Sections of the Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 24 of the Code of the County of Henrico, to Implement Recent Changes in State Law Regarding Marijuana Distribution, Processing, and Retail Sales; Increase Height Limitations in the Form-Based Alternative Overlay District; and Update, Modify, and Clarify Certain Provisions. This Board paper would amend the zoning ordinance in Chapter 24 of the County Code to implement recent changes in state law relating to the creation of a legal retail marijuana market in Virginia; increase height limitations in the Form-Based Alternative Overlay District; and update, modify, and clarify certain other provisions. The Planning Commission recommended approval of this ordinance after a public hearing held on October 15, 2026. The Director of Planning recommends approval of the ordinance, and the County Manager concurs. Ordinance - Vacation of Building Lines and Lot Lines - North Willow Lawn Subdivision - Brookland District. This ordinance vacates the building lines across and lot lines between Lots 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19, Block B, Section A, North Willow Lawn subdivision. The owner of the encumbered parcels has requested the vacation to develop the Willow Circle Apartments. The Real Property Division has processed the requested vacation through the Departments of Planning, Public Works, and Public Utilities without objection. The Director of Real Property recommends approval of the Board paper; the County Manager concurs. 3 Resolution - Condemnation - Easements - Fall Line Trail Longdale Phase Project 1529 and 1551 Mountain Road - Fairfield District. This Board paper authorizes condemnation proceedings for property that is needed for the construction of the Fall Line Trail Longdale Phase project. The County needs to acquire permanent joint use utility easements containing 4,635 square feet across the properties located at 1529 and 1551 Mountain Road and owned by Doswell Ventures, LLC. Based on independent appraisals, the County made an offer of $10,429 for the required property interests, but the parties have not reached an agreement. This Board paper authorizes the County Attorney to institute and conduct condemnation proceedings in accordance with the Code of Virginia. This Board paper further authorizes and directs the County Manager to continue to seek a voluntary acquisition of the easements, to take all steps necessary to acquire the easements, and to enter on and take possession of the required easements in accordance with the Code of Virginia. The Directors of Public Works and Real Property recommend approval of this Board paper; the County Manager concurs. Ordinance - Vacation of Building Line - Pinehurst Gardens Subdivision - 3016 Briar Lane - Fairfield District. This ordinance would vacate the 45-foot building line on Block A, Lot 5, of the Pinehurst Gardens subdivision, also known as 3016 Briar Lane. The owner has requested this action to make improvements to his front porch. The Real Property Division processed the requested vacation through the Departments of Planning, Public Works, and Public Utilities without objection. The Director of Real Property recommends approval of the Board paper; the County Manager concurs. Public Comment General Agenda Resolution - Approval of Participation in Proposed Settlement Agreement Resolving Opioid-Related Claims Against Albertsons Companies, Inc. This Board paper would approve the County’s participation in proposed settlements of opioidrelated claims against Albertsons Companies, Inc. The proposed settlement is anticipated to provide funding of approximately $286,074.61 to the County over nine years The funding will be used to abate the damage caused in the community by the opioid crisis. The Board’s outside opioid litigation counsel has recommended that the Board approve the proposed settlement. The County Attorney recommends approval of the Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. 4 Resolution - Award of Contract - Multi-Cancer Early Detection Testing Services. This Board paper awards a contract to GRAIL, Inc. to provide multi-cancer early detection testing services. Three proposals were received on August 4, 2026, in response to RFP 26-2983-7JOK. After review of the written proposals and oral presentations, the Evaluation Committee selected GRAIL, Inc. as the top-ranked offeror and enter into negotiations for service rates. The Chief of Fire and the Purchasing Director recommend approval of the Board paper, and the County Manager concurs. Introduction of Ordinance - To Amend and Reordain Section 9-2 Titled “Precincts and polling places” of the Code of the County of Henrico to move the Polling Places for the Maplewood Precinct in the Fairfield District from Abundant Life Church of Christ to Harvie Elementary School and the Causeway Precinct in the Three Chopt District from Gayton Baptist Church to Nuckols Farm Elementary School. This Board paper introduces for advertising and public hearing on December 15 an ordinance to move the polling places for (i) the Maplewood Precinct in the Fairfield District from Abundant Life Church of Christ to Harvie Elementary School and (ii) the Causeway Precinct in the Three Chopt District from Gayton Baptist Church to Nuckols Farm Elementary School. These two churches are no longer able to accommodate election activities. The Electoral Board requested approval of this Board paper at its meeting on September 3, 2026. Resolution - Award of Contract - Williamsburg Road and Chapman Lane Water Line Extensions - Varina District. This Board paper awards a fixed price contract of $897,000 to Metra Industries, Inc. for the Williamsburg Road and Chapman

text: AGENDA MIDDLESEX COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION 10/12/2026 7:00 P.M. Call to Order Roll Call 1. Approval of Agenda 2. Approval of Minutes – September 10, 2026 3. Public Hearings 1. Ordinance Amendment #2026-02, to amend the Middlesex County Zoning Ordinance to insert provisions for temporary support structures for wireless communication facilities to effect compliance with the Code of Virginia, §15.2-2316.4:5. 3. Ordinance Amendment #2026-03, to amend the Middlesex County Zoning Ordinance Article 15C, Renewable Energy Facilities and related references throughout the Zoning Ordinance, to effect compliance with the Code of Virginia, §15.2-2241.2, §15.2-2288.7 and §15.2-2288.8, regarding solar energy and battery storage facilities. 4. Ordinance Amendment #2026-04, to amend multiple sections of the Middlesex County Zoning Ordinance to effect compliance with the Code of Virginia, §15.2-2307, §15.22247 and §15.2-2290, regarding manufactured housing. 5. Ordinance Amendment #2026-05, to amend the Middlesex County Zoning Ordinance Article 16, Signs, Section 16.3 to allow a property with the primary use of a church to install one electronically controlled illuminated sign and to add illumination level restrictions for all electronically controlled illuminated signs. 4. Old Business 5. New Business 6. Planning Director’s Report 7. Committee Report 8. Adjournment MIDDLESEX COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION PROCEDURES FOR CITIZEN PRESENTATIONS ON PUBLIC HEARING MATTERS Per the by-laws of the Planning Commission, the following procedures shall be utilized for all public hearings: 1. No person may address the Commission unless recognized by the Chairman. 2. Comments shall be directed to the Commission – not to the audience or the applicant. 3. Each person who desires to address the Commission shall be allowed three (3) minutes to present written and/or oral comments, except that attorneys or agents representing three (3) or more citizens shall be allowed ten (10) minutes. Final rebuttal by the applicant, or their representatives shall be allowed five (5) minutes. These time limits may be changed at the discretion of the Planning Commission. 4. Unless otherwise permitted by the Chairman, each person will be given only one (1) opportunity to address the Commission. PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 AT A MEETING OF THE MIDDLESEX COUNTY PLANNING COMMISSION HELD ON THURSDAY, September 10, 2026 IN THE BOARDROOM OF THE HISTORIC COURTHOUSE, SALUDA, VIRGINIA: Present: Bev Butler, Pinetop District Teresa Anderson, Secretary, Harmony Village District Marilyn South, Hartfield District Russ Perkinson, Harmony Village District Mary Lynn Landgraf, Jamaica District John England, Vice Chairman, Saluda District Tyler Crittenden, Pinetop District Denita Hammond, Jamaica District RD Johnson, Chairman, Hartfield District Tammie Putney, Saluda District Reginald Williams, Supervisor Absent: Joyce Wolfe, Planning Director Jody Collier, Community Development/Building Office Manager CALL TO ORDER Chairman Johnson called the September 10, 2026, regular meeting of the Planning Commission to order at 7:00 P.M. APPROVAL OF MINUTES On a motion by Commissioner Perkinson seconded by Commissioner Crittenden, and carried by unanimous vote, the minutes of the August 13, 2026, meeting were approved. PUBLIC HEARING 1. Special Exception #2026-01, a request by Dan C. Monette, Owner & Applicant, 1 PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 to allow a contractor use as a Special Exception on Tax Map Parcel 19-42A, zoned Low Density Rural, located in the 2100 block of Warner Road in the Jamaica Magisterial District. Chairman Johnson introduced Special Exception #2026-01 Ms. Wolfe presented her staff report recommending approval conditioned on the following: • • • • • The development of the property shall be in substantial conformance with the preliminary site plan titled “Monette Property”, prepared by Bay Design Group, dated July 27, 2026. Hours of operation for the use shall be limited to 7 am to 5 pm Monday through Saturday. Any exterior lighting installed shall be designed to be directed downward, prevent glare onto adjacent properties and shall not exceed .5 footcandles above background lighting at the property line. The storage yard shall not be open to the public. There shall be no trash, litter, debris, junk or construction waste stored on site. Ben Burton, with Bay Design Group, addressed the board on behalf of Dan Monette. He answered questions they had. Chairman Johnson opened the public hearing. With there being no comments, Chairman Johnson closed the public hearing. A motion to approve Special Exception #2026-01 as submitted was made by Commissioner England, seconded by Commissioner Perkinson and carried a vote to approve with nine yes and one abstain. 2. Ordinance Amendment #2026-01, to amend the Middlesex County Zoning Ordinance Article II, Section 11-4, General Business District, to add Tattoo and Piercing Salon as a Special Exception use in the General Business District. Chairman Johnson introduced Ordinance Amendment #2026-01. Ms. Wolfe presented her staff report recommending approval as submitted. Chairman Johnson opened the public hearing. With there being no comments, Chairman Johnson closed the public hearing. 2 PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 A motion to approve Ordinance Amendment #2026-01 as submitted was made by Commissioner Butler, seconded by Commissioner England and carried a vote to approve with eight yes and two abstain. OLD BUSINESS NEW BUSINESS • • On a motion by Commissioner Butler, seconded by Commissioner England, and carried by a unanimous vote, Commissioner South was appointed secretary. On a motion by Commissioner South, seconded by Commissioner Butler, and carried by a unanimous vote, Commissioner Perkinson was appointed to the CIP committee. PLANNING DIRECTOR’S REPORT COMMITTEE REPORTS ADJOURNMENT With there being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Commissioner Butler, seconded by Commissioner England, and carried by unanimous vote. The meeting was adjourned at 7:54 p.m. Respectfully submitted, ___ Theresa Anderson, Secretary Date 3 SE-2026-02, JEREMY HOWARD Special Exception Pinetop Magisterial District Planning Staff Report Overview Applicant Owner Request Current Zoning Tax Map Number(s) Overall Acreage/CUP Area Address Application Submitted Case Advertised Adjacent Property Owner Letters Mailed Planner Jeremy Howard RCS Holdings, LLC Special Exception to permit a tattoo and piercing salon in the General Business District GB, General Business District 30-32-6 .98 acres; 1200 square feet (2 retail units) 2324 Greys Point Road 10/7/26 10/29/26, 11/5/26 10/28/26 Joyce Wolfe Background: At their meeting on October 6, 2026, the Board of Supervisors approved Mr. Howard’s request to amend the Zoning Ordinance, Article 11, Section 11-4, to include tattoo and piercing salon as a Special Exception use in the General Business District. This request is the next step in the process required for Mr. Howard to operate a tattoo and piercing salon at his proposed location in the Rappahannock Crossing retail center located at 2324 Greys Point Road in Topping. Surrounding Development and Zoning The Rappahannock Crossing center is located adjacent to other commercial uses and across Greys Point Road from industrial uses. There is one property, in front of the industrial area that remains LDR zoning. Analysis: Special Exception Criteria: In accordance with Article 7, Section 7-4, Special exception uses shall satisfy all of the following criteria: 1. Shall not be located closer than five hundred (500) feet to any residential district. There is no Residential District property within 500 feet of the proposed use. 2. The property shall abut an existing highway maintained by the Virginia Department of Highways and Transportation. The center fronts on Greys Point Road, a public road maintained by VDOT. 3. Loudspeakers which constitute a nuisance to adjoining properties shall not be permitted. There are no loudspeakers planned with the proposed use. 4. Lighting shall not shine directly on adjacent properties. There will be no outdoor lighting planned with the proposed use. 5. All permitted structures and uses shall be kept and maintained in neat and orderly manner. The proposed use will be in a leased space within the Rappahannock Crossing center. The owner of the center is a party to the application and would be responsible for the exterior upkeep of the building. 6. The use shall not generate noise, smoke, fumes, glare, traffic, or fire hazards which would constitute a nuisance or danger to adjoining properties. The proposed use would not generate noise, smoke, fumes, glare or fire hazards. There will be no significant increase in traffic. Preliminary Site Plan: As the use is internal to an existing retail center and parking is existing, no preliminary site plan was required. County Agency/Department Considerations Building Building Department will be consulted to determine that all code requirements are met for the proposed use ; zoning permits will be required for the accessory storage structures. Public Safety (Police, Fire) No impact expected. Utilities n/a Schools n/a State Agency Considerations Health The proposed use requires VDH compliance with health and safety requirements. DPOR Tattoo & Piercing Salons must have a license issued by the Board for Barbers & Cosmetology; individual artists must possess a DPOR license. VDOT The entrances to the center from Greys Point Road are existing, no further approval is required. Recommendation: Staff recommends APPROVAL of the request for a Special Exception for a tattoo and piercing salon on tax map parcel 30-32-6 in the General Business zoning district subject the following conditions: 1. The hours of operation shall be limited to 11 am to 9 pm daily. 2. A sign permit shall be submitted for any proposed signage for the use. 3. The applicant shall obtain a Middlesex County business license. 4. Once obtained, the Tattoo Parlor license issued by DPOR shall be provided to the zoning office. 5. The use is limited to the proposed 1200 square feet in the Rappahannock Crossing center. Any expansion at the location will require an amendment to the Special Exception. Should the use be relocated to another site, a new Special Exception application will be required. (write in) --- / Via letter(s) sent first class mail on ___l 0---1 r-a_'8--ffu_1o_. / Date Date Commis ion E pires Aerial/Tax Parcel Map Zoning Map Future Land Use Map OA 2026-02; Wireless Communication Facilities Temporary Support Structures Ordinance Amendment Planning Staff Report Overview Initiated by Request Case Advertised Planner Middlesex County Planning Commission/Ordinance Committee Amendment to the Zoning Ordinance to insert provisions for temporary support structures for wireless communication facilities 10/29/26, 11/5/26 Joyce Wolfe Background & Analysis: At their 2026 session, the Virginia General Assembly approved legislation (HB 876; § 15.2-2316.4:5.) to require localities to incorporate into their zoning ordinances, provisions for temporary support structures for wireless communication facilities that meet certain requirements. The bill deﬁnes a temporary support structure as a monopole or portable wireless communications facility used to provide wireless voice, data or image transmission within a designated area for up to 180 days with extensions not to exceed 2 years. The legislation includes the following provisions: • Temporary support structures less than 80’ in height, portable and erected for less than 30 days will not require a building permit; over 80’ or erected for greater than 30 days requires a building/zoning permit application. • Applicant shall demonstrate necessity based on 1)use to tests and evaluate system performance and the need for additional wireless facilities; 2) supplementation communications coverage when an existing facility goes offline due to an accident or natural disaster; 3) supplementation of increased communication needs of the locality due to a declared emergency; 4) supplementation of increased communication needs of the locality for a limited period of time due to a special event held within the locality; or 5) any other reason deemed necessary and appropriate by the locality. • Applicant may request approval for up to 180 days and have the ability to request extensions in writing, with the total time not to exceed 2 years. • Failure of the locality to adopt provisions in its ordinance to implement the provisions shall deem applications granted with no building permit or other permits required. Proposed Zoning Ordinance Amendment: Insert language directly from § 15.2-2316.4:5. 15-30. Wireless Communication Facilities - Temporary support structures. A. All temporary support structures shall require the submission of a zoning permit application; any temporary structure that is 80 feet or less in height, on wheels, and erected for less than 30 days shall not be required to obtain a building permit. B. An application for a temporary support structure shall demonstrate that it is necessary for one of the following reasons: 1. Administering limited frequency and modulation testing to evaluate system performance and the need for additional wireless facility sites; 2. Supplementing communications coverage when a previously permitted wireless facility has become involuntarily non-operational through an accident or natural disaster; 3. A substantial increase in the communications needs of the locality due to an emergency declared by the locality, Commonwealth, or federal government; 4. A substantial increase in the communications needs of the businesses, residents, or visitors of the locality for a limited period of time due to a special event held within the County; or 5. Any other reason deemed necessary and appropriate by the Director of Planning. C. An application for a temporary support structure may request approval for up to 180 days. An extension beyond the initial approval period may be approved if (i) the requests are made in writing prior to the expiration of the initial approval period or current extended approval period, (ii) the extensions are reasonably necessary to resolve or accommodate the reasons for the initial approval, and (iii) the total time approved for extensions, including the initial 180 day period, does not exceed two years. D. Temporary support structure shall be removed at the cost of the owner and the site restored to its previous condition within 48 hours of the end of the approval period. Recommendation: Staff recommends APPROVAL of the request to amend the Middlesex County Zoning Ordinance to add section 15-30 to Article 15: Supplementary District Regulations to incorporate provisions for temporary support structures for wireless communications facilities. PRESENT: ABSENT: SECRETARY: STAFF: COUNTY ATTORNEY: OTHERS: TOM BEEBE, ADAM SANDRIDGE, JAY MELVIN, DAVID WHITMORE ANTHONY SUBRIZI CHRIS SLAYDON NEIL WHITMORE, JASON TYREE, VIVECA HANSON JOHN DRYDEN * * * * * Mr. Beebe called the meeting to order at 7:00 pm and announced that Mr. Subrizi was unable to physically attend the meeting due to being out of town but had the opportunity to participate in the meeting electronically. Due to an illness, Mr. Beebe said that Mr. Subrizi may be absent from the meeting. Mr. Beebe conducted the following verbal roll call: Mr. Subrizi – absent, Mr. Melvin present, Mr. Sandridge – present, Mr. Whitmore – present, Mr. Beebe – present. Mr. Beebe discussed that citizens had the opportunity to participate in the meeting remotely, via Zoom or phone, in addition to being physically present. The instructions for the remote participation options were available on the County website. Those wishing to view the meeting, live or after the fact, could do so on the Rockbridge Planning Commission YouTube channel, also linked on the County website. * * * * * The second item on the agenda was the citizen comment period. Mr. Beebe asked if there was anyone physically present that had signed up to speak. Ms. Hanson said there was no one that had signed up. Mr. Beebe asked if there was anyone wishing to comment via phone or Zoom. Mr. Slaydon said there were no hands raised. * * * * * The third item on the agenda was a review of the minutes from the September 9, 2026 Planning Commission meeting. Mr. Beebe asked if the Commissioners had the opportunity to review the minutes as provided and if there were any questions or comments. At 7:02 pm, Mr. Sandridge made a motion to approve the minutes as submitted. Mr. Melvin seconded the motion. The motion was approved unanimously. 1 * * * * * The fourth item on the agenda was a review of the Board and Committee actions that had taken place during the prior month. Mr. Whitmore reported that following had taken place: - At its October 13, 2026 meeting, the Board of Supervisors reappointed Mr. David Whitmore to serve a new term as a member of the Planning Commission. - At the September 28, 2026 Board of Supervisors meeting, the Board reviewed the proposed zoning text amendment to County Code Chapter 30, Article VII, Section 72, pertaining to solar facilities. The amendment, required in order to comply with recent changes to State Code, was approved by the Board of Supervisors. - Additionally at its September 28, 2026 meeting, the Board of Supervisors reviewed the draft zoning text amendment to Chapter 30, Article III, Section 12 of the County Code to update the definition of Agrivoltaics. The amendment was approved. - Lastly, at its September 28, 2026 meeting, the Board of Supervisors reviewed the draft zoning text amendment to Chapter 30, Article VII, Section 62 of the County Code pertaining to manufactured homes. The Board approved the amendment. - The TCO Board met on October 7 and reviewed the revised site plans for the Circle K convenience store on N Lee Hwy, and the revised plans for Renovating Rockbridge LLC Storage building, near the intersection of Route 11 and Route 39. The TCO Board approved both revised site plans. - The Board of Zoning Appeals did not meet in September. - The Community Development Committee met on September 21, 2026 and reviewed the previous Planning Commission meeting and upcoming Board of Supervisors agenda. * * * * * The fifth item on the agenda was a zoning text amendment pertaining to the use of manufactured homes in various zoning districts. County of Rockbridge, Virginia, 150 South Main Street, Lexington, Virginia 24450 Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) to modify Chapter 30, Article VI, Sec. 30-40B (Permitted Uses in the Residential General District - R-1), Sec. 30-41B (Permitted Uses in the Residential Mixed District - R-2), Sec. 30-42B (Permitted Uses in the General Business District - B-1), Sec. 30-42C (Special Exceptions in the General Business District - B-1) and Sec. 30-45 (Flood Hazard District - FH-1) of the Code to modify the regulations pertaining to manufactured homes. The full text of the draft amendment can be obtained by contacting the Office of Community Development (contact information below). Mr. Slaydon gave a brief overview of the proposed zoning text amendment to the County Code, pertaining to the use of manufactured homes in various zoning districts. It was reviewed that the proposed zoning text amendment was in response to recent changes to Virginia State Code that were enacted during the 2026 Legislative Session. House Bill 655, which went into effect on July 1, 2026, pertained to the zoning requirements for manufactured homes. It was noted that, in addition to the current proposed zoning text amendment, the Planning Commission 2 had previously reviewed and recommended approval of an amendment relating to the manufactured housing regulations for the County. This zoning text amendment was approved and adopted by the Board of Supervisors at their September 28, 2026 meeting. Mr. Slaydon discussed that further updates to the zoning ordinance were required in order to comply with the recent State Law changes. The proposed zoning text amendment applied to Chapter 30, Article VI of the County Code, pertaining to uses in various zoning districts. Specifically, the draft modifications were found in Sections 30-40B (Permitted Uses in the Residential General District - R-1), 30-41B (Permitted Uses in the Residential Mixed District R-2), 30-42B (Permitted Uses in the General Business District - B-1), 30-42C (Special Exceptions in the General Business District - B-1) and 30-45 (Flood Hazard District - FH-1) of the County Code. The Planning Commission reviewed the draft amendments at its August 12, 2026 meeting and instructed staff to take the matter to public hearing at a future meeting. Reviewing the proposed changes, Mr. Slaydon said that while manufactured housing was allowed in the R-1 and R-2 zoning districts under existing Regulations, the proposed modification was to remove the requirement that such homes be at least 19 feet in width. It was discussed that the stipulation in width prohibited the use of a single-wide dwelling in the Residential zoning districts. Mr. Slaydon noted that under the new provisions of the State Law, manufactured homes of any size homes could not be treated differently than a stick-built dwelling. Mr. Slaydon said that in the B-1 zoning district, the Regulations had provisions for one- and two- family dwellings as permitted uses and allowed manufactured homes only as a use by special exception. At the previous direction of the Planning Commission, the draft amendment added the ability to place manufactured homes in the B-1 zoning district as a permitted use while removing it as a use by special exception. Lastly, the proposed modifications extended to the FH-1 zoning district. The existing Regulations allowed for structures to be placed in the FH-1 district as a use by special exception when used in accessory to the permitted uses in the district. However, manufactured homes were not allowed to be used for this accessory structure purpose. The proposal was to remove the statement of exception that disallowed manufactured homes as accessory structures under the use by special exception. Mr. Beebe asked if the Planning Commission had any questions or comments on the draft amendment. Mr. Whitmore asked what Chapter 30, Article VI of the Rockbridge County Code pertained to. Mr. Slaydon said that within Article VI were the regulations for the Uses within Districts, which covered the uses in all districts in the County, from the Agricultural zoning districts to the Conservation zoning district. It was clarified that, of the multiple zoning districts covered in Article VI, the proposed modifications pertained only to the R-1, R-2, B-1, and FH-1 zoning districts. At 7:10 pm, Mr. Beebe opened the public hearing and asked if there was anyone physically present that had signed up to comment. Mr. Slaydon said there was no one that had signed up. Mr. Beebe asked if there were any hands raised via Zoom or phone. Mr. Slaydon said he saw no hands raised. Mr. Beebe closed the public hearing at 7:11 pm and asked if there was any additional conversation. 3 Hearing none, at 7:12 pm, Mr. Whitmore made a motion to recommend to the Board of Supervisors that the proposed zoning text amendment pertaining to the use of manufactured homes be approved by the Board of Supervisors. Mr. Melvin seconded the motion. The motion was approved unanimously. * * * * * The sixth item on the agenda was a zoning text amendment pertaining to the definition of Public Utility Service, Major, and Public Utility Service, Minor. County of Rockbridge, Virginia, 150 South Main Street, Lexington, Virginia 24450, Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA) to modify Chapter 30, Article III, Sec. 30-12 (Specific Definitions) of the Code to update the definitions of “Public Utility Service, Major” and “Public Utility Service, Minor.” The full text of the draft amendment can be obtained by contacting the Office of Community Development (contact information below). Mr. Slaydon provided a brief introduction to the proposed zoning text amendment, which was initiated in order to comply with House Bill 711, that went into effect on July 1, 2026. It was discussed that the amendment to the Code of Virginia imposed restrictions on the local government regulation of solar facilities. Mr. Slaydon reviewed that at its September 28, 2026 meeting, the Board of Supervisors reviewed the draft zoning text amendment to Chapter 30, Article 7, Section 30-72 of the County Code pertaining to Solar Facilities. This amendment was previously reviewed and recommended for approval by the Planning Commission at their August 12, 2026 meeting, in addition to proposed amendments to the Public Utility Service, Major, and Public Utility Service, Minor definitions. The Board’s action, however, did not extend to include the proposed definitions amendments. It was discussed that the notice of public hearings pertaining to the Planning Commission’s August 12, 2026 meeting and the Board of Supervisors September 28, 2026 meeting, properly advertised the amendments to the Solar Facilities Section of the County Code. However, the notices did not extend to include the proposed modifications to the Public Utility Service, Major, and Public Utility Service, Minor definitions. The public hearing at the current meeting was to ensure that the proper advertisements were made prior to the hearing, as required by the Code of Virginia. The full text of the draft amendment was included in the Planning Commission package. Mr. Beebe asked if there were any comments from the Planning Commission. Hearing none, Mr. Beebe opened the public hearing at 7:15 pm and asked if there was anyone physically present that had signed up to comment. Mr. Slaydon said there was no one that had signed up. Mr. Beebe asked if there were any hands raised via phone or Zoom. Mr. Slaydon said there were no hands raised. Mr. Beebe closed the public hearing at 7:16 pm and asked if there was any discussion from the Commission members. At 7:16 pm, Mr. Melvin made a motion to recommend to the Board of Supervisors that the zoning text amendment to the modify Chapter 30, Article III, Sec. 30-12 (Specific 4 Definitions) of the Code to update the definitions of “Public Utility Service, Major” and “Public Utility Service, Minor” be approved. Mr. Sandridge seconded the motion. The motion was approved unanimously. * * * * * The seventh item on the agenda was a discussion pertaining to potential zoning text amendments. The first proposed zoning text amendment that was discussed pertained to potential regulations regarding Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs). Mr. Slaydon reviewed that the discussion regarding ADU regulations was brought about due to recent changes in state law, House Bill 531, which were adopted during the 2026 legislative session, and are set to take effect on July 1, 2027. The amendment related to the use of ADUs in residential zoning districts. Mr. Slaydon noted that staff had prepared draft language that could be utilized pertaining to the use of ADUs. Reviewing past actions, Mr. Slaydon stated that the Planning Commission had previously reviewed Senate Bill 531 at their September 9, 2026 meeting. At that time, discussion was held regarding the required modifications to the Residential zoning district along with the need for regulations pertaining to ADUs for the Agricultural zoning districts. Mr. Slaydon noted that the Residential zoning districts make up approximately 1.5 percent of the County, and the Agricultural zoning districts comprise about 72 percent of the County. It was discussed that the Office of Community Development receives questions pertaining to ADUs, and they are often regarding the Agricultural zoning districts. Draft language for a potential zoning text amendment pertaining to ADUs had been prepared by staff and included in the Planning Commission package. Mr. Slaydon noted that, in Mr. Subrizi’s absence, he had requested that staff provide a copy of his recent email from September 22, 2026, which he had sent to all members of the Planning Commission, with comments on potential regulations for ADUs. It was discussed that, based on the previous directions given by the Planning Commission at their September 9, 2026 meeting, all of the points made in Mr. Subrizi’s comments had already been incorporated into the draft ADU ordinance. The draft ADU ordinance prepared by staff, incorporating the regulations required by State Law and the previous comments of the Planning Commissioners, was included in the meeting package. Mr. Slaydon discussed that the provisions for ADUs would be planned for inclusion into the existing Chapter 30, Article VII, Section 30-75, pertaining to additional dwellings on a single lot. The existing Section of the Regulations included a provision for temporary buildings used in conjunction with construction work. Mr. Slaydon said the proposed amendment included striking the existing language pertaining to temporary buildings and replacing it with regulations pertaining to ADUs. It was discussed that staff would like to receive directions from the Planning Commission regarding the existing draft as presented and return with modifications for review at a future Planning Commission meeting. It was noted that there was currently a blank included in the draft ordinance pertaining to the overall square footage allowance for an ADU, which could be filled in after additional discussion with the Planning Commission. An example of a definition for an Accessory Dwelling Unit was included in the Planning commission package. Mr. Slaydon discussed that, in addition to the draft definition for accessory 5 dwelling unit, additional definitions may be included in the zoning text amendment that do not exist in the Zoning Ordinance. Examples of such terms for which definitions could be added included dwelling unit and two-family dwelling. Mr. Beebe asked if staff was looking for input on the maximum square footage restriction for ADUs. Mr. Slaydon said that 500 square feet had been discussed as the limit on square footage at the previous Planning Commission meeting but welcomed additional discussion. Mr. Beebe said he would hate to place such a restrictive number and suggested the limit for the ADU could be a percentage, potentially 50 percent, of the square footage of the main dwelling. Mr. Beebe noted that the average house size is likely around 2,000 square feet in size. Mr. Slaydon said that, based on research, the average size of a dwelling in Virginia is close to 2,000 square feet. RE: SEPTEMBER 2026 FINANCIAL STATEMENT Mayor Taylor advised that the next agenda item is the presentation of the September 2026 Financial Statement by Town Treasurer Angela Pennington. Town Treasurer Pennington reported that September ended with a $744,000 surplus. She explained that even though the Town remained $2.8 Million behind the prior fiscal year, to date, finances were moving in a positive direction. Town Treasurer Pennington noted that she expected the sales, meals, and lodging tax tickets to be mailed within about a week, which would allow those revenues to begin coming in. She also reported that 5 Section 7, ItemA. those revenues were $77,000 ahead, overall, compared to the prior fiscal year and $309,000 ahead in comparison through August. 9. RE: OLD BUSINESS A. TRAFFIC CALMING BULB-OUTS AT THE INTERSECTION OF WEST MONROE AND NORTH 7TH STREETS Mayor Taylor advised that the next agenda item is a Staff Report by Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Billy Anderson regarding the assessment of and recommendations for the traffic calming bulb-outs at the intersection of West Monroe and North 7th Streets. Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Anderson presented his assessment of the traffic-calming bulb-outs on Monroe Street. He explained that the Virginia Department of Transportation's (VDOT) traffic-calming guidance considers factors such as street classification, average speeds and traffic volume when recommending devices. Director Anderson stated that following an August 27 inspection and discussions with Bristol District engineers, the bulb-outs appeared generally consistent with similar installations and VDOT expectations. He noted that a speed study would be needed to determine their effect on vehicle speeds. Director Anderson stated that the prior erosion concerns had largely stabilized, with only two small areas behind the curb remaining to be addressed. He noted that the bulb-outs may worsen existing stormwater issues because runoff travels a considerable distance without an upstream curb inlet before reaching the intersection. Director Anderson advised that VDOT staff indicated that additional stormwater-control capacity, potentially including an inlet between Seventh and Eleventh Streets, should be considered as broader improvements. He also discussed surface treatments, noting that VDOT commonly uses vegetation or permeable features to manage runoff and limit added impervious area. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "That's the question I was going to ask you about the concrete, is there a difference between paving and concrete, do they give you any suggestions on concrete in there by chance, or just the paving and leave it vegetation." Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Billy Anderson stated that most applications he was familiar with used pervious surfaces, such as grass, vegetation, or landscape stone, rather than asphalt or concrete. He explained that aggregate stone helped slow runoff before it entered an underdrain within the curb island and covered the inlet collection device. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "Okay, thank you." Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Anderson stated that he observed the stormwater features during heavy rainfall and noted that runoff from approximately two blocks, including contributing flow from 11th Street, collected in the gutter pans. He explained that abrupt angles hindered stormwater flow and that smoother transitions could improve their movement around the curb islands. He stated that based on his observations and discussions with VDOT, he suggested replacing the upstream deflection angle with a smooth, reverse-radius “S” curve connecting to the 6 Section 7, ItemA. existing island. Director Anderson noted that this modification would not resolve all drainage issues and could temporarily direct water farther into the street, but might reduce runoff entering Seventh Street, collecting in the flat area north of Monroe Street, or flowing onto the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) ramp. He also noted that larger street improvement projects could provide opportunities to increase stormwater collection upstream. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "I would like to ask a question to see if Council would entertain a thought to place stone there instead of you know the grass, just for safety for the employees, and I know there's a little part out there at the Food City that possibly may be grass and didn't know if we could choose putting stone there to save, you know, save on mowing and equipment, and also the safety for employees. Is there any way that we can look into putting some stone in there." Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Anderson stated that he participated in a Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) stormwater inspection at Scott Memorial Middle School (SMMS), earlier in the day. He noted that landscape stone used at SMMS, along North Street behind Spiller Street, frequently displaced onto roads and sidewalks, creating obstructions and requiring Town staff to collect and return it to the landscaped areas. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "With the new school." Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Billy Anderson advised that landscaping stone could be difficult to maintain at the site. He commented that during heavy rain, smaller river stones may wash away more readily than grass and collect on sidewalks or in the street, requiring staff cleanup. Director Anderson noted that traffic may also dislodge the stone. He remarked that while stone is an attractive landscaping option, it has maintenance drawbacks and that the existing grass may be more resilient. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "What would be your opinion, probably just leave it." Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Billy Anderson recommended retaining the existing grass, which he stated was likely the most resilient treatment for the bulbouts. He noted that only a small strip near the curb remained eroded and suggested filling and reseeding it during a dry period. Director Anderson commented that the grass appeared consistent with the type VDOT recommends for roadside ditches exposed to similar water flow. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "In the same way as Food City, probably just grass it." Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Billy Anderson inquired of Councilwoman Atkins if she was referencing to the stone islands along West Main Street at Food City. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "The ones right as you, I don't want to take the wrong term now, you know we've all driven it the same way, but they're just 7 Section 7, ItemA. there's like a little section, and then there's like concrete, like a sidewalk, there's just a very little, teeny-weeny section." Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Billy Anderson advised that the landscaped islands along West Main, between the sidewalk and parking lot, are outside the Town’s rights-of-way and are the property owner’s responsibility to maintain. He noted that he had observed the landscaping company mowing the area and picking up litter. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "I'm sorry, no, sir, it's right there at the like at Hope, there's a little like here's Hope, and then here's like I guess an empty lot, there's like a little, I can show you sometime, I can send you pictures, okay." Director of Public Utilities and Engineering Billy Anderson advised that each option had advantages and disadvantages, noting that vehicles driving over landscape stone could displace it into the street. He recommended considering a curved transition beginning farther upstream where stormwater strikes the curb to reduce the obstruction and help water flow around the curb bulb-outs. Councilwoman Atkins stated the following: "Thank you, Mr. Anderson." Mayor Taylor inquired if there was a motion to approve Town staff's recommendation to retain the existing bulb-outs, with modifications to the two upstream connection points where the northerly bulb-outs meet the existing linear curb. These modifications will replace the sharp angles with more gradual curves to improve stormwater flow around the bulb-outs and reduce the tendency for stormwater to overtop the curbs until larger-scale stormwater system improvements are implemented. Motion made by Vice-Mayor Johnson, Seconded by Councilman Hand, Jr. Mayor Taylor inquired if there was any discussion on the motion. RE: PERSONAL PROPERTY TAX RELIEF ACT REIMBURSEMENT RATE Mayor Taylor advised that the next agenda item is a Staff Report by Town Treasurer Angela Pennington regarding the proposed establishment of the Personal Property Tax Relief Act reimbursement rate at 34.43 percent. Town Treasurer Pennington explained that Personal Property Tax Relief is calculated annually using the Town’s state allocation of $61,075.92, which had remained unchanged for years. She stated that the funds must be distributed among eligible vehicles assessed in the Town’s Personal Property Tax file. Town Treasurer Pennington advised that the Wythe County Commissioner of the Revenue’s 2026 file included 469 more vehicles than the 2025 file, requiring the same funding to be distributed among more vehicles. She advised that as a result, the Personal Property Tax Relief percentage decreased from 37.69% in 2025 to 34.43% in 2026.
